newsitem.title: USA: USG gasoline, diesel moves trigger refinery fears.
newsitem.headline: USG gasoline, diesel moves trigger refinery fears.

text.p: High refinery operations and strength in the U.S. Gulf (USG) premium-grade gasolines and low sulphur diesel markets this week kept traders there focused on possible refinery unit outages.

The thinly-traded USG prompt 93-octane conventional V1 gasoline's premium to the regular conventional M1 barrels jumped about 1.00 cent earlier this week to about 6.00 cents, before slipping back to about 5.50 cents.

That strength has been helped by the outage at an alkylation unit at Citgo's Corpus Christi, Texas, refinery after a fire May 12. The company said the fire remained under investigation and no restart date for the unit has been set.
Prompt premium reformulated D1 gasoline also gained about 0.50 cent to sit nearly 5.50 cents over the July NYMEX gasoline before slipping back to 4.75 cents Thursday.
Rumors of other reformer problems in Gulf Coast refiners emerged, though no particular companies appeared to be driving prices higher.
"The premiums have been strong for a while," one trader said, "and that does point to possible reformer problems."
"We can't continue to do that high of refinery runs," another Gulf Coast player said. "Never does it happen that we run this high and nothing goes bump in the night," he added.
The American Petroleum Institute put refinery operations at a brisk 98.3 percent of capacity for the week ended June 6, down 0.1 percentage point from the previous week.

Low sulphur diesel prompt differentials at the USG gained about 0.30 cent earlier this week to sit near 1.50 cents under the July NYMEX heating oil, also raising suspicions of a refinery production problem, traders said.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
